To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a video-on-demand storage server can improve throughput by scheduling the video with the largest factored queue length (MFQ) rather than the video with the longest queue length (MQL) or the video that arrives first (FCFS), and that the weighting factor used to compute factored queue lengths should be a function of the popularity of the videos.

we propose a new batching policy, MFQ, that uses factored queue length to schedule videos, we show that MFQ performs significantly better than the conventional FCFS and MOL policies, and we show how to determine the optimal factored queue length weights.

we have proposed a new batching policy, called MFQ, that is based on factored queue lengths and that this new policy yields superior performance in terms of average latency time, average defection rates and average fairness.
